notes:
## 0.2.206

owes: new collection `stocks.shared_news` (server-owned, shared tier, pulled only; no protocol change and no schema migration) and a news fetch: each symbol a holder follows has its feed fetched once, on that holder's `address_news_feed` with `s=<symbol>` appended, at the stocks interval and never multiplied for a closed market. Nothing is fetched until a news feed address is set, and an older phone ignores the collection (SPEC-097 B14).
owes: **`SYNCHUB_ARTICLE_RETENTION_DAYS` now also bounds `stocks.shared_news`**, by the hub's own write stamp and with no tombstone, exactly as it bounds feed articles. Unset (the default) still keeps everything, so nothing changes until an operator sets it; one that has set it will see news purged on the same window (SPEC-097 B14).
owes: none — `/stocks/news` and `/stocks/news/{articleHandle}` are new, the stocks drawer lists News and the instrument page shows five headlines; the caller's own read and star marks are written to `stocks.news_state`, a per-user collection the phone already pulls, and a phone's *saved* mark is carried through untouched (SPEC-097 B15).
owes: none — `rss/FeedSanitiser` and `rss/ArticleHandles` moved from `:app-feed` to `:hub`, package unchanged, so `:app-stocks` sanitises through the same allow-list; no behaviour change and no new jar in the image.
owes: none — `/weather/settings` now writes the refresh interval (`refresh_interval_hours`, a whole number of hours 0–168) and the source order (`source_order`, `PAGE,DWD` or `DWD,PAGE`) as sync records in the caller's own tier, in the payloads the phone already writes, so the phone pulls them on its next round; an empty field tombstones the key and the hub default applies again. No new collection, no schema migration, no configuration key (SPEC-122 B15).
owes: `/settings/backup` is now the snapshot page and the full archive (database, blobs, file area) is gone — a snapshot holds configuration only (accounts, paired devices, file-area tokens, settings), never records or attachments, so back those up from the data volume. A snapshot is taken daily at a live snapshot time (default 03:30, hub local; catch-up within five minutes of a start that missed it) and on *Take a snapshot now*; 3 daily and 2 monthly are kept, manual ones never pruned (SPEC-047).
owes: new restart setting `SYNCHUB_SNAPSHOT_DIR` (default `snapshots/` beside the database, created at start). The default shares the data disk and the page warns about it; to keep copies off it, mount a second volume (`compose.yml` carries a commented `/snapshots` line) and point the variable there. An unwritable directory is shown as a failure on the page, never a crash loop (SPEC-047).
owes: restoring a snapshot from the browser stops the hub, so the container's restart policy must start it again (`restart: unless-stopped` in the shipped `compose.yml`); it takes a safety snapshot first, replaces the configuration tables, deletes every session and mints a new `generation`, so everyone signs in again (SPEC-047).
owes: new `hub_state` keys `generation` (32 lowercase hex, never snapshotted, never shown), `SNAPSHOT_TIME`, `SNAPSHOT_INCLUDE_FILES`, `snapshot_last_failure`, `snapshot_last_failure_at` and `restore_last_failure`; the old `backup_count`, `backup_last_instant` and `backup_last_size_bytes` rows are no longer read. No schema migration, so a rollback still starts; the restore marker `restore-pending.json` is a new file beside the database (SPEC-047).
owes: schema migrations V029 (`weather_sensor_hours`) and V030 (`weather_forecast_snapshots`) — forward-only; a database that has run them is refused by an older image, so a rollback after the first start needs a backup taken before it (SPEC-120).
owes: new `hub_state` keys `mqtt.host`, `mqtt.port`, `mqtt.tls`, `mqtt.fingerprint`, `mqtt.username`, `mqtt.password` (sealed under `SYNCHUB_SECRET_KEY`; without it a password cannot be stored, and a restore under another key reads `refused_auth`) and `mqtt.discovery_prefix` — all set from Settings → Sensor broker, empty host = off, so nothing changes until an administrator sets one (SPEC-120).
owes: new collection `weather.shared_accuracy` (server-owned, shared tier, pulled only; no protocol change) and the browser-only `shell.local_web` fields `accuracyWindow` and `accuracyField`; an older phone ignores the former (SPEC-120).
owes: the forecast archive in `weather_forecast_snapshots` cannot be re-fetched, so it stays in backups and a restore that predates it loses the history it held (SPEC-120).
owes: new library `org.eclipse.paho:org.eclipse.paho.client.mqttv3` 1.2.5 in `:hub` (the tenth approved dependency); the image grows by its jar, and a hub with a broker host set dials that one operator-chosen address (SPEC-089 §12.10).
owes: none — `com.mambocoding.stocks:core` re-pinned 0.5.19 → 0.5.23; DataCore's notes for that interval all read `none` for SyncHub.
owes: none — SPEC-076: comments, KDoc, build-file and workflow comments now cite the renamed `SPEC-NNN-*.md` files instead of the former `SPEC*.md` names; no behaviour change.
owes: none — stage 2 of Tooling SPEC-01: the hooks, the release workflow and the local release script now run from the tooling/ submodule at v0.1.1; the local copies are deleted.
owes: none — stage 1 of Tooling SPEC-01: the tooling/ submodule, tooling.conf and a hand-run rehearsal workflow; the existing hooks and release.yml are unchanged.

A served app that is switched off no longer sends anyone to `SYNCHUB_MODULES`, `compose.yml` or a
restart: its page says to ask an administrator to switch it on in Settings → Apps, an admin gets the
link to that screen, and the records-already-synced diagnosis keeps its count but drops the variable
(the variable has been ignored since the switch moved into the hub — SH25-01).
owes: none — a message change in all five languages; nothing to configure or migrate.

A body that ends early or is reset mid-transfer is now a `network_error` feed failure instead of an
uncaught exception, so the feed waits its interval like any other failed fetch instead of being
re-dialled every minute (SH25-02). A successful fetch is recorded before the image and article-text
harvesters run, and each harvester is isolated, so an error in one is logged and never leaves the
feed looking never-attempted (SH25-30).
owes: none — behaviour of the fetch loop only; no key, collection or migration changes.

Build only: the three distributions (`:server`, `:desktop`, `:client`) compute their disambiguated `lib/`
names lazily, so configuring any other task no longer resolves their runtime classpath (SH25-03, the
resulting `lib/` file names are unchanged); `generateVersionProperties` declares the version as an input
(SH25-04); stale comments in the build files and `.env` are corrected (SH25-05); the vendor and hosting
platform names are removed from code comments and `GITHUB_REPO`/`fromGithub` become
`RELEASE_REPO`/`fromReleaseHost` (SH25-06).
owes: none — no image content, key, default or URL changes.

The sign-in limiter decides atomically: the pessimistic row, the address lock and the account delay
come from one database block, so a burst of concurrent guesses from one address verifies at most five
times and a burst against one account gets strictly increasing delays (SHS25-24). The account's delay
is served before the single verification permit is taken, so one account under attack no longer stalls
every other sign-in and step-up (SHS25-01). A locked attempt no longer leaves a row behind, so the
five-failure address lock ages out on its own window exactly as before.
owes: none — no schema, key or default changes; existing `login_attempts` rows are read as they were.

`login_attempts` is pruned once a day: rows outside the address window that no longer change any
account's delay are dropped — everything before an existing account's latest success, and every row
naming no account (SHS25-05). The delay an account is serving, and every address lock, are unchanged.
The last prune is stamped under the `login_attempts_prune_last_at` key of `hub_state`.
owes: none — no schema change; the first prune runs soon after the first start on this build.

`POST /login` answers 403 to a request another site made — `Sec-Fetch-Site` neither `same-origin` nor
`none`, or an `Origin` whose host is not the one the hub was addressed by — and does not count it
against the address (SHS25-02). `POST /logout` sends `Clear-Site-Data: "cache"`, so cached note
renditions, feed images and article text leave the browser at sign-out (SHS25-28). A script or `curl`
sending neither header signs in as before.
owes: none — no key, collection or default changes; a reverse proxy that rewrites `Host` but leaves
the browser's `Origin` alone would now see 403 on sign-in, and is the one thing an operator could hit.

A new account's name is NFC-normalised and trimmed, and refused unless it is 1 to 64 characters with no
control character and no `:` (SHS25-08); existing accounts keep whatever name they have. An admin's
password reset or second-factor reset aimed at the admin's own account answers 403 — the step-up on
Settings → Account is the only way to change one's own (SHS25-27); the same posts for another account
work as before.
owes: none — no schema or key change; nothing an operator has to do.

A device's pairing label is stored and logged as at most 64 characters with control characters removed,
and its `app` only when it is 1 to 32 characters of `[a-z0-9._-]` (SHS25-14). The blob and file-area
upload caps in Setup are refused above 2048 MiB, the routes' own body backstop, so a huge number can
no longer overflow the byte count into a negative cap (SHS25-23). A cap already stored above 2048 MiB
is not touched.
owes: none — no key or schema change; only a value someone types above 2048 MiB is now refused.

A WebDAV download names its file with an ASCII `filename` fallback plus RFC 5987's `filename*` for the
exact UTF-8 name, the same encoder the notes attachment download already used (SHS25-15); a name with
a quote or backslash can no longer break out of the header.
owes: none — a response-header change only; no key, collection or default changes.

The mDNS responder answers a unicast query only when its source lies in a subnet of the interface it
is bound to (RFC 6762 §11, SHS25-13); a legacy-unicast or QU query from a routed or spoofed source
gets no reply, and multicast answers are unchanged. Discovery on a normal LAN behaves as before.
owes: none — no key or default changes; nothing to configure.

A request body that is malformed or of an unsupported type — a truncated JSON push, a `text/plain`
body — now answers `400` (or `415`) instead of `500`, and prints nothing. An unhandled exception's log
entry is the method, the matched route and the class names of its cause chain: no message and no
stack trace, which quoted the parser's input or a file path (SHS25-04). A sync client that treated the
old `500` as "retry later" now sees `400` for a body it could never have got right.
owes: none — no key, collection or default changes; the log line loses its message and stack trace,
so an operator debugging from the container log reads class names and the route instead.

A notes attachment is rendered inline only when the decoder its bytes select is the one its declared
media type names: a BMP, a TIFF or a JPEG declared `image/png` answers `404` on `/view` without being
decoded, and the page draws the download row (SHS25-07). A rendition already cached for such a file
stays until the blob is purged — renditions are keyed by the file's digest alone.
owes: none — no key, collection or default changes; a correctly declared PNG, JPEG or GIF renders as before.

The feed image decoder hands its input only to an `ImageIO` reader whose format is PNG, JPEG, GIF or
BMP; a TIFF or WBMP reader is refused before `setInput` and `read`, so it never runs over a fetched
file (SHS25-26). Those files were already refused as images; the decoder for them no longer runs.
owes: none — no stored image, key or default changes.

Build only: the Gradle wrapper pins the SHA-256 of the distribution it downloads
(`distributionSha256Sum`), so a tampered or corrupted `gradle-9.7.1-bin.zip` fails the build instead of
running (SHS25-16). The checksum is now actually in `gradle-wrapper.properties` (gradle-9.8.0-bin.zip,
from services.gradle.org's published `.sha256`); the entry above had been written before it landed.
owes: none — no image content, key, default or URL changes; a Gradle bump must now update the checksum with the URL.

The desktop reader refuses to pair when the pasted `synchub://pair` URI names a certificate fingerprint
and the hub presents another, before the user is asked to confirm and before any code is sent
(SHS25-29). Its data directory is created `rwx------` and `replica.sqlite` `rw-------` where the
filesystem is POSIX, and an existing directory is tightened at start-up (SHS25-30).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; no key, collection or default changes.

Build only: `gradlew` is recorded executable in git (mode `100755`), so `./gradlew` runs on a fresh
Unix checkout without a `chmod` first (SH25-18).
owes: none — no image content, key, default or URL changes.

The desktop reader no longer ends its window when the hub cannot be reached while it fetches a
thumbnail or an article's text: an unreachable hub, a certificate that is not the pinned one, or a bad
stored address answers "nothing to show", so the row keeps its summary (SH25-19). Thumbnails are
requested at the hub's live `feeds/image/{key}` route instead of the legacy `image/{key}`, which
answers a redirect the pinned client never follows, so they now appear (SH25-23).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; no key, collection or default changes.

The desktop reader applies each pulled page of records in one transaction: a failure part-way leaves
the replica exactly as it was, instead of half a page applied behind a cursor that has not moved
(SH25-24).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; the replica schema is unchanged.

The desktop reader's remaining user-visible sentences — the offline banner, the no-browser message,
the default device name and the empty-state sentences — now live in its one English catalogue
(`ClientStrings`), so the other locales can follow in stage 2 (SH25-26).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; the wording is unchanged.

The desktop reader re-reads its replica after every sync round that reached the hub — the article lists,
the feed list and the theme — so what the phone just pushed appears without a restart, and a re-read no
longer resets the article being read (SH25-20). A device whose first attempt could not reach the hub
still shows "waiting for the first sync round", not an empty list, until a round has succeeded
(SH25-20). `j`/`k` scroll the list to keep the focused article in view (SH25-36). An article body's
` ` and numeric character references (`’`, `—`) are decoded instead of shown as
written (SH25-34).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; no key, collection or default changes.

The desktop entry tier's *Start with the system* writes its launch command in double quotes: the
Windows `Run` value holds `"C:\Program Files\SyncHub\SyncHub.exe"` (checked against `reg.exe`, which
strips the quotes of a plainly quoted argument, so the value's own quotes are escaped), and the Linux
`Exec=` is XDG-quoted, so an install path with a space launches at login instead of failing (SH25-27).
owes: an installation that enabled *Start with the system* on an earlier build holds an unquoted value;
it is rewritten at the next launch with the preference on, so nothing needs doing unless the path has a
space and autostart has been silently failing — then start the application once.

The Host guard reads the allowed-hosts setting from memory on every request instead of asking the
database each time; a live setting is cached once it has been resolved at start-up or written through
its own route, so an edit in Setup still takes effect at once (SH25-28).
owes: none — no key, schema or default changes.

The article-text harvester guards its shared bookkeeping and no longer dials one article twice when the
fetch loop and a manual refresh run at once; it also reserves each host's next dial slot, so two
concurrent callers cannot dial the same publisher together (SH25-31).
owes: none — behaviour of the fetch path only; no key, collection or migration changes.

Page messages fill their `{0}`, `{1}` placeholders in one pass, through one helper the hub's and the
four apps' catalogues share, so a feed title or note name that itself reads `{1}` is shown as written
instead of being substituted again (SH25-32).
owes: none — a message change in every language; nothing to configure or migrate.

A note body saved from the web editor is stored with LF line endings: a browser submits a text area
with CRLF while the phone stores LF, and the merge read the two spellings of the same text as a
divergence and minted a conflict copy of equal text (SH25-37). A note already stored with CRLF keeps it
until it is next saved from the browser.
owes: none — no key, collection or schema change; no conflict copy already minted is touched.

Build only: the image's builder stage is `eclipse-temurin:17-jdk`, the toolchain every module compiles
with, so no JDK is provisioned from the network during an image build; the runtime stage stays
`eclipse-temurin:25-jre` (SH25-17).
owes: none — the runtime image's contents, keys and defaults are unchanged.

Build only: the version catalog's comments no longer retell each repin — one or two lines per
`com.mambocoding.*` pin say what it is, and the library's own `specs/RELEASES.md` says what a repin
owed; every version is unchanged (SH25-16).
owes: none — no image content, key, default or URL changes.

The desktop entry tier can no longer strand itself: Settings → Setup's bind step refuses
`127.0.0.1` and no longer offers it, since the entry tier already binds that address itself for its
own window; the window opens on the port its hub actually bound, not a value re-derived from
configuration; and *Apply and restart* re-boots the hub in the same process and re-points the window
only if the port moved, instead of leaving the desktop with no hub at all (SH25-22).
owes: none — desktop reader only, never in the image; no key, collection or default changes.

**About reloads itself after Apply update.** Pressing *Apply update* used to leave the operator
refreshing Settings → About by hand, and a refresh that landed while the hub was being recreated
showed the browser's own connection-refused page. About now loads one small script of its own, only
while a request is outstanding, which polls a new status route (`GET
/settings/about/apply/status`, admin-or-updater, `{"version", "pending"}` and nothing else) every
three seconds, tolerates the hub being down, and reloads the page once the version changes or the
request is no longer pending — giving up after ten minutes with a sentence saying so (UR-01, UR-02).
owes: none — no configuration key, no migration, no collection, no changed default.
